Session 6 lab exercise: Survival Analysis part 1

Levi Waldron

session_lab.Rmd

Learning objectives

  1. Calculate Kaplan-Meier estimates of survival probability over time
  2. Plot survival curves for censored time-to-event data
  3. Perform and interpret log-rank test
  4. Define “informative” censoring

Load the leukemia 6 MP clinical trial dataset

In this dataset, time is weeks until relapse or censoring, and cens is the event indicator: 1 if the patient relapsed and 0 if they were censored. Despite its name, cens = 1 means an event, not a censored observation. We set Placebo as the reference group.

library(tidyverse)
library(survival)
library(survminer)
leuk <- read_csv("leuk.csv") %>%
  mutate(group = factor(group, levels = c("Placebo", "6 MP")))
table(leuk$group, leuk$cens)
##          
##            0  1
##   Placebo  0 21
##   6 MP    12  9

Surv() combines time and event status into a single outcome. Censored times are printed with a +:

with(leuk, Surv(time, cens))
##  [1]  6   6   6   7  10  13  16  22  23   6+  9+ 10+ 11+ 17+ 19+ 20+ 25+ 32+ 32+
## [20] 34+ 35+  1   1   2   2   3   4   4   5   5   8   8   8   8  11  11  12  12 
## [39] 15  17  22  23

Calculate the follow-up table for 6 MP patients

summary() of a survfit object gives the follow-up table: at each event time, the number at risk, the number of events, and the Kaplan-Meier estimate of survival with its 95% confidence interval. Compare this to the follow-up table in the lecture.

fit6mp <- survfit(Surv(time, cens) ~ 1, data = filter(leuk, group == "6 MP"))
summary(fit6mp)
## Call: survfit(formula = Surv(time, cens) ~ 1, data = filter(leuk, group == 
##     "6 MP"))
## 
##  time n.risk n.event survival std.err lower 95% CI upper 95% CI
##     6     21       3    0.857  0.0764        0.720        1.000
##     7     17       1    0.807  0.0869        0.653        0.996
##    10     15       1    0.753  0.0963        0.586        0.968
##    13     12       1    0.690  0.1068        0.510        0.935
##    16     11       1    0.627  0.1141        0.439        0.896
##    22      7       1    0.538  0.1282        0.337        0.858
##    23      6       1    0.448  0.1346        0.249        0.807

Plot the Kaplan-Meier estimate for both groups 

fit <- survminer::surv_fit(Surv(time, cens) ~ group, data = leuk)
survminer::ggsurvplot(fit,
           xlab = "Time (weeks)",
           ylab = "Survival Probability",
           risk.table = TRUE, risk.table.col = "strata")

What is the time by which 25% of patients in each group have relapsed?

This is the time at which the estimated survival probability drops to 75%. quantile() of a survfit object returns quantiles of the event time distribution, so this is the 25 column: the time by which 25% of patients have had an event, and 75% are still event-free.

quantile(fit)
## $quantile
##               25 50 75
## group=Placebo  4  8 12
## group=6 MP    13 23 NA
## 
## $lower
##               25 50 75
## group=Placebo  2  4  8
## group=6 MP     6 16 23
## 
## $upper
##               25 50 75
## group=Placebo  8 12 NA
## group=6 MP    NA NA NA

25% of 6 MP patients had relapsed by 13 weeks, compared to 4 weeks for Placebo patients. The 75 column is NA for the 6 MP group because the Kaplan-Meier estimate never drops below 25% survival before follow-up ends.

Perform a log-rank test comparing the two groups 

survdiff(Surv(time, cens) ~ group, data = leuk)
## Call:
## survdiff(formula = Surv(time, cens) ~ group, data = leuk)
## 
##                N Observed Expected (O-E)^2/E (O-E)^2/V
## group=Placebo 21       21     10.7      9.77      16.8
## group=6 MP    21        9     19.3      5.46      16.8
## 
##  Chisq= 16.8  on 1 degrees of freedom, p= 4e-05

Cap follow-up times at 20 weeks

Suppose you were instructed to cap follow-up times at 20 weeks. Anyone still event-free at 20 weeks becomes censored at 20 weeks, and events after 20 weeks are no longer counted.

leuknew <- leuk %>%
  mutate(newtime = pmin(time, 20)) %>%
  mutate(newcens = ifelse(time <= 20, cens, 0))

Kaplan-Meier plot:

fit20 <- survminer::surv_fit(Surv(newtime, newcens) ~ group, data = leuknew)
survminer::ggsurvplot(fit20,
           xlab = "Time (weeks)",
           ylab = "Survival Probability",
           risk.table = TRUE, risk.table.col = "strata")

Log-rank test:

survdiff(Surv(newtime, newcens) ~ group, data = leuknew)
## Call:
## survdiff(formula = Surv(newtime, newcens) ~ group, data = leuknew)
## 
##                N Observed Expected (O-E)^2/E (O-E)^2/V
## group=Placebo 21       19       10      8.05        14
## group=6 MP    21        7       16      5.05        14
## 
##  Chisq= 14  on 1 degrees of freedom, p= 2e-04

Give a hypothetical example of how censoring in this example might be “informative.”

If sicker patients were moved to another hospital where they weren’t followed up on, and were also more likely to relapse, this would be informative censoring.

Exercises

Exercise 1: Median survival and median potential follow-up time

Using the uncapped data, find the median survival time and its 95% confidence interval for each group by printing fit. Then estimate the median potential follow-up time for each group using the reverse Kaplan-Meier method from the lecture, where censoring is treated as the “event”: survfit(Surv(time, 1 - cens) ~ group, data = leuk). Why is the median potential follow-up time NA for the Placebo group? Is there any reason to believe potential follow-up differed between the two arms of this trial?

Exercise 2: Cumulative event function

Plot the cumulative event function 1−S(t)1 - S(t) for both groups by adding fun = "event" to ggsurvplot(). Using summary(fit, times = 10), estimate the proportion of patients in each group who had relapsed by 10 weeks.

Exercise 3: Effect of capping follow-up

Compare the log-rank test from the uncapped data to the one capped at 20 weeks. How did the observed and expected numbers of events, and the chi-square statistic, change? Explain why capping follow-up changed the result, even though the Kaplan-Meier curves before 20 weeks are identical.
